data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Idempotent operations satisfy f(f(x))=f(x): repeated application converges to the same state as a single application. Safe operations merely cause no corruption or harm when repeated, but their repeated state may differ from the single-application state. An append-only event log requires only that its writers be safe\u2014retried appends produce duplicate entries but no corruption\u2014while idempotency is deferred to the replay processor, which must deduplicate (via sequence numbers, idempotency keys, or hash-based collapsing) to achieve deterministic replay.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log's consumers cannot distinguish duplicate entries from originals (e.g., no idempotency keys, no sequence numbers, no content hashing), then safe-but-non-idempotent writers are insufficient and the log effectively requires idempotent writes via upstream deduplication","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If deterministic replay is defined as byte-for-byte log identity rather than semantic state convergence, then duplicate entries from retries break determinism and the log requires idempotent writers with idempotency keys","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the downstream processor is not itself idempotent (e.g., a counter increment), then safe writers alone do not suffice\u2014every duplicate entry corrupts the replayed state","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An append to the log is inherently non-idempotent: appending the same event twice yields two entries, a different state from appending once. But it is safe: the log tolerates duplicates without corruption, violating no invariant. Deterministic replay survives because the replay layer applies idempotent processing semantics downstream\u2014it collapses or ignores duplicates. The writer's obligation is merely retry-safety (don't corrupt the log on retry); the system's obligation is idempotent consumption. This separation is why at-least-once delivery is compatible with deterministic replay: safety at the write boundary, idempotency at the replay boundary.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
